title: The sages take refuge
hookLine: an old sage rises from the fire, and the sages show Rama why they need someone to run to: the start of sharanagati
carry: sharanam: whoever takes refuge is protected

cards: Sharabhanga asks Rama to wait and watch. He builds a fire, makes the offering of clarified butter, and with the words of the rite, steps into the flames. Rama, Sita and Lakshmana stand there.
The old body burns away. And out of the fire, Valmiki says, rises a young man, shining, who goes up to the world of Brahma. The sage had waited only for this: to see his guest, and then to go.

teach.b: It's important to say what this scene is and isn't. Sharabhanga is a great ascetic at the very end of a long life of tapas, already invited to heaven.
The text presents his entry into the fire as a sacred departure, a completed life, not a despairing one.
If thoughts of ending your own life ever come to you, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, or call local emergency help. Then the mood changes.
The sages gather around Rama, ascetics of every kind, some living on water alone, some on air.

teach.h: A PILE OF BONES IN THE FOREST.
teach.b: They lead him to a place where bones are piled up: sages killed by rakshasas, the man-eating demons of Dandaka. This is what happens to us, they say. We have no protector.

teach.h: WE COME TO YOU FOR REFUGE.
teach.b: We come to you for refuge. And Rama answers, with no one ordering him to: I'll destroy those who harm you. Here is one of the deepest ideas in Hindu devotion: sharanagati, taking refuge in God.
You come with nothing and say: I'm yours, protect me. Later, in the war, Rama makes it a vow: whoever comes to me even once and says I am yours, I keep safe from every being.
Many Hindu prayers lean on one word, sharanam, refuge. It's in a grandmother's whispered Ram on a dark night. And here, by a pile of bones, Rama first says yes.

how: Ramayana reciters tell Sharabhanga's departure with reverence, and Rama's promise to the sages here sets up the battles later in the Aranya Kanda.

games.q: you're Rama. the sages show you a pile of bones and say: we have no protector. what do you do?
o: tell them to leave the forest.
promise to destroy the rakshasas who harm them.
say your exile is only to keep a promise.
games.why: Rama promises to protect them. they came for refuge, and he said yes: sharanagati. later, Sita will ask him whether that promise was wise.

practice: Fold your hands at your chest, the way Hindus do before God: the gesture of someone who comes with nothing. Think of one fear you're carrying, and hold it honestly for a moment.
If you pray, say sharanam, refuge, or simply I'm yours, on each out-breath, and hand the fear over. If you don't, breathe out slowly and name one person you could take it to.

wordCard.voice: Sharabhanga. The old sage who rose from the fire to Brahma's world. After him, the sages come to Rama for refuge, and he promises to protect them.
